accident_report:
Vehicles V1, V2, V3, and V4 are traveling on a straight, downhill, one-way roadway consisting of three lanes, with a wide shoulder on the right side. V1 is in lane 2, positioned ahead of the others, moving steadily at 85 km/h with the intention of maintaining its lane. V2 follows directly behind V1 in the same lane at a distance of approximately 10 meters, traveling at 90 km/h, intending to continue forward without changing lanes. V3 is in lane 1 (rightmost lane), slightly behind V2 by about 5 meters, traveling at 70 km/h, maintaining a constant speed. V4 is in lane 3 (leftmost lane), slightly behind V2 by about 8 meters, traveling at 100 km/h, intending to overtake slower vehicles. The road surface is wet due to ongoing heavy rain, reducing tire grip, and visibility is moderately degraded.

As the vehicles descend the slope, the downhill gradient causes all vehicles to naturally accelerate if not actively controlled. V1 encounters a slight accumulation of water on the road surface and reduces speed from 85 km/h to 70 km/h by applying moderate braking to maintain stability on the wet surface. Due to the wet road and reduced friction, V1’s deceleration is gradual but noticeable. V2, following too closely at only 10 meters and traveling faster at 90 km/h, has insufficient time and distance to respond smoothly. Upon observing V1’s brake lights, V2 applies hard braking; however, the wet surface significantly reduces braking efficiency, causing V2’s speed to drop sharply but with extended stopping distance.

Meanwhile, V4 in lane 3, traveling at 100 km/h, observes V2’s rapid deceleration and initiates a lane change to lane 2 to overtake before fully assessing the reduced speeds ahead. Due to the speed difference and wet conditions, V4’s lateral maneuver reduces its stability. At the same time, V3 in lane 1 maintains 70 km/h but begins to slightly accelerate to 75 km/h due to the downhill slope, approaching the rear-right side of V2.

As V2 continues heavy braking, its rear begins to experience slight instability due to the wet surface. V4, merging into lane 2, is forced to brake abruptly upon realizing V2’s reduced speed. The combined effect of high speed, wet pavement, and downhill momentum causes V4 to lose partial traction. V3, observing V2’s braking and V4’s encroachment, attempts to maintain its lane but reduces speed slightly to 68 km/h.

The critical moment occurs when V4, unable to stabilize in lane 2, closes the gap rapidly and collides with the rear-left side of V2 at approximately 60 km/h, while V2 has slowed to around 50 km/h. This collision constitutes the first impact, triggered by the combined effects of close following distance, significant speed differences, downhill acceleration, and reduced tire-road friction due to wet conditions.
